Dear Folks and Ruth: Received quite a BIT of stuff from you this week. First I received finally that package of developer paper that you sent me several months ago. Came thru in good condition the and stild OK to use. But the sad package came in the same mail and that consisted of one good phonograph record broken to bits. I'm afraid we didn't have much luck with that shipment and will have to try again. You made the mistake of packing the box too loosely so that if anything fell on the xbox it was sure to hit the record. I believe that you said that additional shipments are on the way. I'm crossing my fingers for the next one. I sent home several snapshots during the past week which I trust you have received by now. Am inclosing another group in this envelope of natives fishing on the shores of a large lake. Also received you(weekly letter telling of the newest development in the house ownership situation.....Things are getting very busy here and am spending more time than usual at my work. Ever since the Philippine operations began we have really had our problems. And each one a tremendous one too. It's required a great deal of work on the part of all of us. Perhaps I'll be able to explain all that was involved when we see each other again. The way our news of European developments are coming in that may be a reality sooner than we expect. Todays headlines contained the wonderful news of the allied rejection of the first German peace offer. They soon will have only to take and offer nothing but compliance with unconditional surrender terms. It shouldn't be too long after hitler falls that things over here will come to a showdown. Even at that we are doing pretty well for ourselves in the south pacific. Today theres a big rugby game going on outside and the shouts are going big guns. That's one of England's and Aust traditional games and they play it with real zest.. It's a rather crude version of our game of football and about that dangerous for the players. Don't recall telling you that I received a letter from Abe and he's quite bright about things in general or at least appears that way. But I guess you are better acquainted with his set-up than I. Mail is still trickling in slowly here. Spent an enjoyable day last week working with some of the officials from the Dutch government with regard to money of theirs that is being used by the US army in this theater. They invited us up to One of their clubs in town and it was all a very enjoyable experience. There are quite a few Dutchmen in Brisbane both military and civilians who have come from the Dutch East Indies. They are a very congenial people, and speak a brand of English that is pretty hard to understand. I had quite a time conversing with one of them in French. That is about all the news that I can salvage for you out of the weeks doings. So until next week Love and regards [illegible]
